items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: I still have in my possession ... a letter from Bob Weinstock to Thelonious Monk releasing him of his contractual obligations to Prestige.

ctx.x: No, I wanted to make sure what you were taking about.

Fine. Okay. The world has gone on to other forms of waylaying people. I mean I’m not old enough to have been around when the press gangs were kidnapping sailors and putting them on ships in the harbor, but this is almost it. But no the point is so what I’m saying is it’s a combination of a certain amount of osmosis. Pop music was in the air to a very large extent and it was very close to being or actually was jazz at this point, and then also physical circumstances made it possible for me to have direct listening…

in those days that I did not realize the impossibility of what I wisely set out to do, but on the spot it was a big, sprawling Greenwich Village studio living room, Monk and I went off into a corner disregarding all the other people there and I interviewed him for an article that appeared in the magazine. ctx.x: Wes Montgomery. Yes. Actually, I guess when you’re putting things in order; it’s Bill Evans and Wes Montgomery that stand out as an art. They are just a matter of my being told about somebody and having followed up on it. That sequence of events thing that I was starting to talk to you about with the presence of Clark leading to the Adderely’s, and the really the next step in that story is Cannonball coming into my office one morning.
